headline_marked: No passport needed for [[Hasina to be handed over]] from India
headline: No passport needed for Hasina to be handed over from India
summary: State Minister Humaiun Kobir dismisses suggestions that former PM Sheikh Hasina needs travel documents to return as a fugitive under an extradition treaty.
details: State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that Bangladesh wants former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to be handed over by India under an existing extradition treaty.
Responding to questions at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the minister dismissed the idea that she would require a passport or other travel documents to facilitate her return.
Kobir described Hasina as a 'terrorist' and 'fugitive,' arguing that no legal requirement exists to issue travel documents to someone being arrested and handed over through a judicial process.
He mocked the idea of a passport, asking if she were visiting her in-laws' home in Rangpur, emphasizing that passports are not needed to arrest criminals.
The minister confirmed that Bangladesh will continue to pursue her return through established legal and diplomatic channels.

Separately, the minister also discussed the potential of a Bangladesh-Myanmar-China Economic Corridor, noting that stability and a solution to the Rohingya crisis are prerequisites for the initiative.

State Minister Humaiun Kobir says no passport is required for the extradition of Sheikh Hasina.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that Bangladesh wants former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to be handed over by India under an existing extradition treaty.

Responding to questions at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, the minister dismissed the idea that she would require a passport or other travel documents to facilitate her return.

Kobir described Hasina as a 'terrorist' and 'fugitive,' arguing that no legal requirement exists to issue travel documents to someone being arrested and handed over through a judicial process.

He mocked the idea of a passport, asking if she were visiting her in-laws' home in Rangpur, emphasizing that passports are not needed to arrest criminals.

The minister confirmed that Bangladesh will continue to pursue her return through established legal and diplomatic channels.

Separately, the minister also discussed the potential of a Bangladesh-Myanmar-China Economic Corridor, noting that stability and a solution to the Rohingya crisis are prerequisites for the initiative.

headline: 78 police inspectors promoted to ASPs in sweeping move
summary: The government has inducted 78 police inspectors into the Bangladesh Civil Service (Police) cadre in a single move.
details: The government has promoted 78 police inspectors to the rank of assistant superintendent of police (ASP).
This move inducts them into the Bangladesh Civil Service (Police) cadre in a single sweeping action.
The home ministry issued three separate notifications on Thursday to announce the promotions.
The promoted officers' services have been placed under Police Headquarters.
The orders take effect immediately for all 78 inspectors named in the notifications.
